**What this PR does / why we need it**:

From https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-windows/20190103-windows-node-support.md#v1container

Windows container does not have a root user,but kubelet will still check the user of the windows container when creating the pod.

The current inspection conditions are based on the `RunAsNonRoot` and `RunAsUser` of the Linux container, and the results checked based on these conditions are incorrect

From a sig-windows perspective, I wonder if it makes sense to bar `runAsUsername` from being `ContainerAdministrator` (https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/configure-pod-container/configure-runasusername/). `ContainerAdministrator` does somewhat emulate `root` user in Linux contexts. Let's discuss this is a bit in sig-windows (if it has not been already).
@ddebroy let me know the outcome of the sig-windows discussions.  I can approve once sig-windows has decided how to handle this.

> We [discussed this at sig-windows today](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Tjxzjjuy4SQsFSUVXZbvqVb64hjNAG5CQX8bK7Yda9w/edit#) and came to the consensus we should be more restrictive initially as it will be hard to constrain later. Rather than ignore `RunAsUserName` we should block when the user is `ContainerAdministrator`.

Of course, I can try to change. Originally I planned to participate in this sig-windows discussion too, unfortunately I missed it due to time constraints. I will go to watch the video on youtube, the details of your discussion, and then make changes
thanks! feel free to ask questions in the sig-windows slack channel if you have any

issue_context.title: PodSecurityPolicy rule: 'MustRunAsNonRoot' and windowsOptions: runAsUserName not working
issue_context.body:
Hello, 

**What happened**:
When we apply PodSecurityPolicy with rule:

```
runAsUser:
    # Require the container to run without root privileges.
    rule: 'MustRunAsNonRoot'
```

WIndows containers are still blocked instead we put: 

```
  securityContext:
   windowsOptions:
      runAsUserName: "ContainerUser"
```

the pod is still blocked with logs: 

`  Warning  Failed          1s (x10 over 72s)  kubelet, kubenodewin04  Error: container has runAsNonRoot and image will run as root `

**What you expected to happen**:

the Container should start

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Create Psp disableling Root Users:

```
runAsUser:
    # Require the container to run without root privileges.
    rule: 'MustRunAsNonRoot'
```

Create a pod Windows with runAsUserName:

```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: run-as-username-pod-demo
spec:
  securityContext:
    windowsOptions:
      runAsUserName: "ContainerUser"
  containers:
  - name: run-as-username-demo
    image: mcr.microsoft.com/windows/servercore:ltsc2019
    command: ["ping", "-t", "localhost"]
  nodeSelector:
    kubernetes.io/os: windows
```

**Anything else we need to know?**:

**Environment**:
- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`): v1.18.3
- Cloud provider or hardware configuration: 
- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`): CentOS Linux 7 (Core) / windows server 2019 version 1809
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):  3.10.0-514.10.2.el7.x86_64
- Others:
/sig windows

review_comments: Do you want to report a warning or error if `*effectiveSc.RunAsUser` was set to some (any) value? This configuration may indicate an intent to configure security that cannot be satisfied on windows
Adding this warning message is indeed friendly for windows

linux version of this method will return nil here. Meaning that if `WindowsOptions.RunAsUserName` was set to a value that is not root, it will OK that independently from values of `uid ` and `username `. Why is this one different?

Already fixed
The logic of linux container is to judge by the security context of pod and container first, if the user does not input, judge by mirror metadata. Windows reuses this logic
the pattern in file naming is `security_context_windows.go` and `security_context.go` In couple places I saw `_unix` or `_linux` suffices. I'd vote for consistency and drop `_other`

Here I have a very uncertain thing is that other platforms besides Linux and Windows support this feature, so I chose to use others~~

There are many examples of this in kubernetes,such as
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/pkg/kubelet/apis/config/validation/validation_others.go

thank you for pointing out. Somehow all examples I saw was not using this pattern. I guess it's ok. If not previous examples my suggestion would be `security_context_non_windows.go`. It may be the most descriptive name

About this, I went to look at some of the existing designs of kubernetes.

- If the platform support is very clear, it is generally `*_linux.go`, `*_windows.go`, `*_unspport.go`. 
- If it is possible to distinguish between windows and others, it is generally `*_others.go`, `*_windows.go`.

I think it’s better to follow the existing naming rules, otherwise it will confuse people , what do you think?
sure, lets keep it. It looks consistent with the pattern. Thank you for looking into it
same in `security_context_test.go`?
I didn't get what you meant.

the file security_context_test.go calls into the method you modified. If you compile different version on windows - running these tests on windows would fail. So I suggest to add the same `build !windows` to the file containing tests
Also worth renaming the test file with the same pattern as the product code. With `_other` or `_non_windows` suffix.
changed.

This is a big deal, right?  Someone thinks they are running with security options that we aren't applying.  Should this fail more loudly?

If i'm interpreting this correctly, I would suggest emiting an event, or even returning an error here.  Same comment for other unsupported options.

I think the argumentation here is that these settings were likely set by some plugin. See https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93475#discussion_r486666465

This is why warning was good enough from my perspective, but I'd like somebody from windows sig to confirm

Because these do not cause cri errors, it is just that the features of linux container on windows container cannot take effect, and vice versa. If kubelet fails more loudly, it will affect existing applications (adding wrong WindowsOptions or LinuxOptions). So I think the warning level log may be a way to make sense (may need to be more detailed)

> Maybe we should add a check to https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/360659102c8ae94a5bee6e9cbbc3d1160db58428/pkg/apis/core/validation/validation.go#L3769 that verifies only one of SecurityContext.SELinuxOptions or SecurityContext.WindowsOptions are set.

Tightening API validation is not generally possible (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/64841). If that combination of settings is never legitimate (is a multi-OS image possible?), we could add that to the list of things we want to warn about (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/94626)
Thanks @liggitt, that addresses my concern.
This also addresses my concerns as well and I agree a warming would be more appropriate here.
